Manual

Playing it

ControlWhat it does
FX SEL ENV LFO EDIT GLO (top row)choose layer 1 2 3 4 5 6. The chosen layer's button is lit; the others glow while they sound.
PRESETS knobthe chosen layer's engine: FM, ANIMA or CALIGULA, left to right. Each layer keeps a sound of each engine, so turning back finds the sound it had.
HOMEa new sound for the chosen layer, on its engine (never the same family twice in a row). HOME lights for a moment.
OCT− / OCT+the chosen layer's octave, −3 to +3. OCT− is lit below the middle, OCT+ above.
the white keysplay the chosen layer in the scale chosen (ARP): the first white key is the root, each white key the next note of the scale, up across all 16. Two voices per layer: a new note never cuts the release of the one before it — a third note takes the voice that has rung longest. A key lifted ends its note on the layer it was played on, so a held note keeps sounding while you choose and play another layer. The keys you hold on the chosen layer light up.
the rightmost black keySHIFT (lit while held; each press shows the audio's load in % of the time it has, now / at most since the last press, e.g. LOAD 62/91). Hold white keys and press SHIFT: they latch — they keep sounding after you let go, and their keys stay lit. Hold SHIFT and press a lit key to let go of it.
the two leftmost black keysthe chosen layer's generative path: the first AMBIENT, the second EXPERIMENTAL (lit while chosen; the screen says which). Pressing the lit one again goes back to OPEN. See below.
the other black keysplay no notes (kept for other functions to come).
ARPthe SCALE page (ARP lit): SELECT chooses the root (C to B), ALGORITHM the scale. The root is shown very large, the scale under it; what you just turned flashes black on white. ARP again, or a layer button, goes back.
RECthe chosen layer's looper. Press to arm a new loop (REC flashes, the band shows ARMED and its number); the first note you play starts it (REC lights; REC and the number). Press REC again to end it: the loop is exactly as long as from that first note to this press, and it starts playing at once, round and round. Press REC again while it plays to overdub: the same again, a new loop over the others — up to 10 loops a layer.
REC held (1 s)empty the chosen layer's looper, all its loops: the whole screen flashes LOOP n / EMPTY.
PLAYstop the chosen layer's loops, or play them again, each from its start. PLAY is lit while they play. SHIFT and PLAY, from any layer: if any loop plays, every loop on every layer stops (LOOPS OFF; the loops are kept); if none plays, every loop there is starts, all together from their starts (LOOPS ON). PLAY alone still starts or stops the chosen layer's own.
SELECT knobthe chosen layer's level: 1.5 dB a click, from OFF up to +4.5 dB. The message band says it as the knob's share of its turn, OFF and 4 % to 100 % (VOL 74 %); a layer starts at 87 % (0 dB).
KNOB 1the chosen layer's DJ filter: from the middle (off), left is a resonant low-pass coming down from 20 kHz to ~35 Hz, right a resonant high-pass going up from 16 Hz to ~12 kHz; the further from the middle, the more resonant. While you turn it, and for a second after, the whole screen is its dial (in the layer's colour, the mode and cutoff under it: LP 1.2 KHZ). Saved with the session.
KNOB 2the chosen layer's granulator: the middle is off (as it starts). Left towards dark ambient: long, overlapping, slowly drifting grains, pitched down now and then, darkened, fed back on themselves, sometimes frozen. Right towards scattering: short, fast grains, their timing, place, pitch and level jittered more and more, reversed, stuttered, full of holes, decimated at the far end. The further from the middle, the more grains and the less of the layer. While you turn it, the whole screen is its dial (DARK 40, SCATTER 25, OFF). Saved with the session.
KNOB 3the chosen layer's crush: the middle is off (as it starts). Left takes the bit depth down from 16 to 1.5 bits (the sound coarsens, then breaks up, quiet tails gating out); right takes the sample rate down from 44.1 kHz to ~300 Hz (metallic aliasing, then a stepped buzz). Both along curves that keep the first half of the way playable; the rate glides, it does not jump. While you turn it, the whole screen is its dial (BITS 6.5, RATE 2.6K). After the granulator, before the layer's limiter. Saved with the session.
KNOB 4the chosen layer's reverb send, 0–100 (40 at the start). While you turn it, the whole screen is its dial (SEND 40), as for the filter and the granulator.
SAVEthe SESSIONS page: PRESETS turns through the 64 slots (the number shown very large: red when the slot holds a session, faint grey with EMPTY under it when it does not; the session loaded says LOADED). SAVE on a saved slot loads it; on an empty slot it chooses it (the sound stays as it is) so the next save goes there. Either way back to playing. A layer button goes back without either.
SAVE held (0.8 s)save into the session loaded or chosen, at once; the whole screen flashes SAVED and the number. With none loaded or chosen yet (just after switching on), the first empty slot is offered: PRESETS chooses NO / YES, SAVE answers. On the SESSIONS page, SAVE held saves into the slot shown, whatever is loaded: an empty one asks SAVE NEW; one holding a session asks OVERWRITE? in red, on NO until PRESETS turns it to YES; SAVE answers.
SEQthe REVERB page (SEQ lit). There KNOB 1–4 are SIZE, DECAY, DAMP, MIX. SEQ again, or a layer button, goes back.
ALGORITHM knobthe chosen layer's pan, left to right in 41 steps. The message band says it (PAN L 50, PAN C). Layers start spread out: 1 and 2 half left and right, 3 and 4 a quarter, 5 and 6 near the middle.
USB MIDI innotes play the chosen layer, as the keys do.
MASTERthe level.

Generative paths

Each layer has a path that leans what HOME draws, on every engine. A path changes nothing already playing: it shapes the next sounds drawn on that layer. The path's key is lit while that layer is chosen.

PathKeyLeans towards
AMBIENT1st black keysounds for ambient, dark ambient above all: ethereal, melodic, often melancholic. FM draws drones, beating spectra (SPECTRE), the depths (ABYSS) and bells, never BRUIT, IMPACT or FRICTION; then softer attacks, long tails, darker modulators, slow LFOs, no sirens, narrower glides, often an octave down. ANIMA draws mostly HAZE, GOLDEN and VOYAGE, never GRIT, with a darker tone, more space, a slower hand, long releases, no crusher. CALIGULA draws SPORE and VEIL most, CARRION, sometimes RUST; tuned on root, fifths, octaves, depths and unisons; slow swells, softer edges, fewer bursts and surges, a slower hand
EXPERIMENTAL2nd black keysounds for electroacoustic and acousmatic music: edgier, gnarlier. FM draws bruits, frictions, impacts and iterations, brighter, mutated more often (sometimes twice), never SPECTRE. ANIMA draws mostly GRIT and SWARM, never HAZE, and makes them wild: the sliders near their tops (FM, grain, texture, density, a quick hand), the resonance often screaming, and on most designs a crushed sample rate, folding drive, a band of noise and scattered grains, all dragged about by the hand, often a fast tremolo tearing it apart, the comb ringing hard. CALIGULA draws THORN, HIVE and RUST most, never VEIL; semitone clusters and tritones; sharper, more driven, more bursts and surges, a quicker hand
OPENneither litevery family, kind and species alike, as before the paths. Every layer starts here

Sessions keep each layer's path, and the path each of its sounds was drawn on.

Latched keys

Hold one or more white keys and press SHIFT (the rightmost black key): they latch, sounding on after you let go, and they stay lit. A key pressed while SHIFT is already held plays as usual (unless it is lit). Latches belong to the layer they were made on: the keys are lit while that layer is chosen, and on another layer the same keys play as usual, so a drone can be left on one layer while you play another. Pressing a latched key without SHIFT does nothing (it sounds already); SHIFT and the lit key lets go of it, and its note ends as a lifted key's would. Loading a session lets go of every latch. A layer has two voices, so a third note takes one of them, even a latched one's.

The loopers

Every layer has its own looper of up to ten loops, and they are all free: no tempo, no grid, no quantising — not even between a layer's own loops. Each overdub is a loop of its own, as long as you made it (from its first note to REC), going round in its own length over the others, so they drift in and out of phase. Each plays back exactly what was played, to 0.73 ms. The keys go on playing the layer over its loops, and the loops' notes and the keys' never cut each other's notes off — but all of them share the layer's two voices, so many loops at once take voices from each other. A layer's loops hold about 1000 notes between them; nothing is lost when the FM-1 is switched off if the session is saved.

The screen

From top to bottom: the layer number (very large, in the layer's colour), its engine (FM or ANIMA, in white), the family of its sound (in the layer's colour). When something changes (NEW, OCT +1, LOOP), a black-on-white message replaces the family for a moment. While the chosen layer's looper is armed the band below the engine flashes ARMED in red; while it records it shows REC, white on red. A message too long for the band at its usual size (EXPERIMENTAL) is drawn a size smaller. Under it, across the screen, the layer's level meter: a bar filling from the left with the layer's colour as it sounds (-48 to +6 dB), and a white mark at the level the SELECT knob sets (red at the left when the layer is off). At the very bottom, the layer's pan: a block in its colour on a track from left to right, with a tick at the middle.

KNOB 1 to 4 (filter, granulator, crush, reverb send) each show, while they turn and for a second after, the same full-screen dial: the knob's name and the layer, an arc from 7 to 5 o'clock lit in the layer's colour, a white pointer, and in large type what it does.

The REVERB page shows the title and its four values in rows, each with a bar; the row you just turned is drawn black on white for a moment.

Scales

One scale and root for the whole keyboard (and saved with the session); C major at the start. The root sits on the first white key, in the octave from C3 to B3 (each layer's OCT moves it); the scale climbs from there across the 16 white keys, so a pentatonic scale spans more than three octaves.

ScaleSteps
MAJOR0 2 4 5 7 9 11
MINOR NATURAL0 2 3 5 7 8 10
MINOR HARMONIC0 2 3 5 7 8 11
MINOR MELODIC0 2 3 5 7 9 11
DORIAN0 2 3 5 7 9 10
MINOR PENTA0 3 5 7 10
WHOLE TONE0 2 4 6 8 10
ENIGMATIC0 1 4 6 8 10 11
JAPANESE IN0 1 5 7 8 — the in (miyako-bushi) scale of the koto and shakuhachi, known for its sorrow

USB MIDI notes are not quantised.

Sessions

The FM-1 always starts with no session loaded. There are 64 slots, numbered 1–64.

A session stores in full the sound of the engine each layer is on, and the other two as the seed that made them and their level (the same sounds, drawn again at once), so a session usually takes one 4 KB sector of flash. A session is the whole machine: every layer's engine and its three sounds, its path, octave, level, pan, reverb send, filter, granulator, crush and loops (playing or stopped); the scale and root, the reverb, and the layer chosen. They are kept in the FM-1's flash, in the area SLOOP uses for its projects (saving overwrites any SLOOP projects, presets and samples left on the device): dozens of typical sessions, at least ten even with six full loops. A session also keeps the seeds its sounds were made from, so it still loads (with the same sounds) after a firmware update changes how sounds are stored. Erasing flash silences the audio for a moment: a save uses blank flash when there is some, and the FM-1 blanks free flash by itself while nothing sounds.

The granulator

Each layer keeps the last half second of its own sound (at 22 kHz, 8-bit mu-law: a little grit is part of it) and plays grains out of it, after its filter. Each layer's granulator has a character of its own, drawn at random when the FM-1 starts and every time a session is loaded: the intervals its grains are pitched to, how often they reverse, stutter, drop out or freeze, the shape of its scattered grains, how far its feedback and darkening go, how it drifts. The knob's position is saved with the session; the character is drawn anew. When the layer's notes end, its grains ring on for about two seconds.

The reverb

A plate after Jon Dattorro (1997): predelay, input diffusion, and a figure-of-eight tank whose two allpasses sweep slowly out of step, so the tail stays in motion and never rings. Each layer sends to it after its level; the reverb's return is added to the mix before the master.

at the start
SIZEthe room: every delay 0.5–1.25 times Dattorro's (turning it bends the tail, gently)70
DECAYthe time to fall 60 dB, 0.4 s to about 25 s, whatever the size65 (about 3.5 s)
DAMPhow fast the highs die in the tail40
MIXthe reverb's return level, ×0 to ×450 (×1)

Layer colours: 1 yellow, 2 cyan, 3 pink, 4 green, 5 orange, 6 lilac.

The engines

FM — six operators, DX7 style

The classic six-operator FM (msfa, the core of Dexed: 32 algorithms, rate/level envelopes, ratio or fixed frequencies, feedback, LFO, pitch envelope). HOME draws a patch from one of nine families of sound objects:

FamilyAfter
METALbells and gongs: many carriers on inharmonic ratios, the high partials dying first
DRONEspectral drones: near-harmonic pairs detuned to beat, an index wandering over minutes
BRUITnoises: feedback and high ratios scattered by a sample-and-hold LFO
IMPACTstruck bodies, the pitch falling, the modulators dying before the carriers
ITERATIFiterative objects: a sound pulsed by its own LFO, square or random
GLISSEglissandi: a pitch envelope travelling octaves, slowly
SPECTREa spectral arpeggio: rich tones a few cents apart whose beating lifts one harmonic after another
ABYSSsub-bass rumble folded by feedback, breathing slowly
FRICTIONcreaking: sub-audio fixed-frequency modulators and random pitch

About one patch in three is then mutated once more (a partial nailed to a fixed frequency, an envelope turned over, the feedback pushed, the LFO taken too far, an octave away, another family's algorithm). Every patch is rendered offline as it is made and given the gain that brings it to one loudness.

ANIMA — a synthesizer played by a simulated hand

A fixed-point port of the anima opcode from Vascular, rebuilt for the FM-1. While a key is held, a simulated finger rests on a virtual surface and drags one figure after another — orbits, figures of eight, scribbles, slow glides, now and then a flick — pressing in slow swells, and now and then lifting to land elsewhere. A ghost finger comes and goes on an irregular clock. Where the finger is, how hard it presses, how fast it moves and how long it has been down move the timbre, never the pitch.

The voice: two wavetable oscillators (24 band-limited single cycles), an FM pair, a stack of copies, a grain cloud, a filtered noise, a resonant filter, a wavetable tremolo; then the hand's chain: a downsampler, a waveshaper, a phaser, a second filter and a comb resonator tuned to the note. Each new sound is a design: which of these are in, on which waveforms, and for every parameter which gesture moves it, over what range, along what curve, plus a mod matrix of three to seven routes and Anima's eight sliders, drawn — often far from their middle. Eight kinds: HAZE, VOYAGE, GLASS, BELLS, GOLDEN (Anima's own) and BREATH, GRIT, SWARM (made for this firmware).

In Vascular a design plays up to six fingers, each a voice; here a layer has one voice, so the hand has one finger on the sound.

CALIGULA — an organism

The third engine, after the architecture of SOMA's LYRA-8 as Mike Moreno's LIRA-8 emulates it (BSD licence), rebuilt for the FM-1 and bent towards dark, restless textures. Eight oscillators in four pairs on two sides; each a triangle that its pair's SHARP pushes towards a square; each with a sensor and an envelope, slow (a long swell, a longer fall) or fast; each pair frequency-modulated at audio rate by its partner, the other pair of its side, a pair of the other side or the total feedback (the whole organism, saturated, fed back in). A hyper LFO of two LFOs (alone, AND, OR, XOR) opens and closes the modulation and gates chosen pairs into irregular rhythms; a short modulated delay (two lines, ~35 ms) choruses, flanges or warps it; a drive.

A CALIGULA layer is played like the others: the white keys play the scale's notes, and it is silent until a key is down. A key wakes the organism at that note; a second key on top moves the whole organism to the new note at once (a snap, not a glide), and letting go of it goes back to the key still held; letting go of the last key lifts the hand and the organism rings out. It is rooted: tuned around the note played, in intervals of it (octaves, fifths, unisons and semitone clusters that beat, tritones, the depths). The hyper LFO moves timbre, never pitch: no sirens.

Nobody touches the eight plates: a simulated hand does, while a key is held. Each species has its own hand: how often it touches, how long a finger stays, how many fingers at most, its favourite plates, quick taps against long holds. The first finger stays down until the key is let go, so the sound never drops out under a held key. Around the hand the organism has a life of its own: the modulation depths and the sharpness wander, oscillators fire in bursts at irregular times, and now and then the feedback and the drive surge for a moment. A pair's envelope may be slow: a swell of seconds, a release of up to nine seconds after the key is let go. HOME draws a new organism from six species:

Species
SPOREslow swells, held drones, breathing; low
THORNsharp, deep FM, driven, bursting often
HIVEthe hyper LFO quick and gating: irregular rhythms, bursts
CARRIONthe depths, heavy total feedback, the delay warped by the voices, surges
VEILmostly triangles, light modulation: the calmest
RUSTdriven, cross-modulated, surging, sometimes rhythmic
